decisions.reason: As a relatively core psychiatric-care extension with a dedicated page, it still has option value in 2024 despite meaningful staffing costs and should be kept while demand becomes clearer.

A custom-furniture carpentry workshop sits comparatively far from the core residential-care business and likely ties up space and supervisory resources, so weak early evidence would justify abandoning it.
Outpatient sociotherapy is adjacent to the firm's care capabilities and can be kept as a low-to-moderate cost option even though its limited website prominence suggests an early-stage test.
Counseling for senior living is highly aligned with the firm's main market and its home-page placement signals strategic importance, so management would be likely to continue it.
A retail shop linked to a sheltered workshop is mission-related but commercially peripheral and probably vulnerable to thin margins, making it a plausible candidate to close if traction is modest.
